newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWIMMING-MAGANOS SETS PACE IN EUROPEAN SHORT-COURSE CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-MAGANOS SETS PACE IN EUROPEAN SHORT-COURSE CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Greek swimmer Dimitrios Maganos upstaged more fancied rivals to lead qualifiers in men's 400 metres freestyle heats on the opening night of the European sprints and short-course championships on Thursday.
Maganos, an 18-year-old medical student who won a gold medal at the Schools' World Cup in 1994, took the first heat in three minutes 48.94 seconds. He is coached in Athens by Briton Clive Rushton.
Italy's Emiliano Brembilla, fourth in the Atlanta Olympic 400 freestyle final in July, was third-fastest overall of the six qualifiers for Friday's final in Rostock's Neptun pool.
Brembilla clocked 3:51.09 to finish second in his heat behind Germany's Stefan Pohl (3:50.91).
Russia's Alexei Stepanov, fifth at the distance at the 1995 European long-course championships, eased through his heat and made the final with something to spare.
Scheduled heats for the women's 800 freestyle were cancelled, the event resolving itself into a final on Friday because there were only five entrants.
German Kerstin Kielgass pulled out of the event following an appendix operation last Friday. Olympic finalist Kielgass is one of several leading swimmers absent from the meeting.
The inaugural championships in this former East German Baltic port city pick up pace on Friday when the first 13 of 38 finals are decided. They end on Sunday.
